answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying each identity to a refundable stake locked behind verified work, not a free signup. Reputation is like copper wiring: cheap to claim in bulk, costly to keep live. Before high-value trade, an agent must complete small, checked tasks over time, building a basalt-solid history peers can audit. If it cheats, its stake is slashed and its record marked. Forging a thousand identities then means funding a thousand bonds and repeating a thousand voyages of real work, turning a free identity flood into a slow, expensive, easily detected investment.
